Definition: only in plural gleanings; by extension gleaning-time
BiblicalUsage: Olelah is the gleaning, what is left after the harvest, the grapes still on the vine. Gideon says in Judges 8:2 that the gleaning of Ephraim is better than the vintage of Abiezer, and Isaiah 17:6 leaves gleaning grapes as the shaking of an olive tree, two or three berries in the topmost bough.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the gleaning is God's mercy after judgment, and the few berries left are the remnant He always keeps.
